Sammed Shikharji: Parasnath Hill's Jain Heritage

Parasnath Hill (Chapter 1's highest point) hosts Sammed Shikharji, one of Jainism's most sacred pilgrimage sites — according to Jain tradition, 20 of the religion's 24 Tirthankaras (spiritual teachers), including Parshvanath (after whom the hill is named), are believed to have attained moksha (liberation) at this site, making it arguably the single most sacred site in all of Jainism.

The site has been the subject of recent (2023) controversy after a Jharkhand government notification proposing to develop the area as an 'eco-tourism' destination drew strong protests from the Jain community nationwide, who argued this could compromise the site's sanctity (given Jain dietary and lifestyle prohibitions around activities like alcohol consumption, non-vegetarian food, and general tourism-related disturbance in a site considered a place of pilgrimage rather than casual tourism) — the notification was subsequently put on hold following the protests and central government intervention.

★ EXAM POINT: The 2023 Sammed Shikharji eco-tourism controversy is a notable and frequently tested current-affairs-cum-religion topic for Jharkhand — remember it centred on tension between tourism-development plans and the site's status as Jainism's most sacred pilgrimage site (associated with 20 of 24 Tirthankaras attaining moksha there).

items: Baidyanath Dham (Deoghar) — one of the twelve Jyotirlingas (sacred Shiva shrines) of Hinduism, making it one of Jharkhand's most significant Hindu pilgrimage sites and a major annual pilgrimage destination during the Shravani Mela festival period.
Rajrappa Temple (near Ramgarh) — a significant Shakti Peetha-associated temple dedicated to Chhinnamasta Devi, at the confluence of the Damodar and Bhairavi rivers.
Palamu Forts (Chapter 2) — historic ruins of the medieval Chero dynasty's fortifications, now within Betla National Park.
